deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. Σ is a finite arrangement of n pseudo-lines in the real projective plane X, with S its set of vertices (crossing points). X̃ → X is the 2-sphere double cover. D is a further pseudo-line, either in general position with respect to Σ or 'special', meaning it passes through some vertices ω ∈ S. D̃ is the preimage of D in X̃, a circle. Each ω ∈ D∩S has two lifts ω', ω'' on D̃.

The objects studied are the combinatorial (isotopy) classes of such D relative to Σ. They are related by immediate specializations D → D', in which D is pushed across a vertex until it passes through it. The coloured sketch shows exactly this: the green line D collapses a triangle formed with two orange lines, and the dashed green path runs along the two orange sides into their crossing point. The reverse move is a generization.

Left column. Conversely, a specialization of D at a vertex ω corresponds to an oriented arc of D̃ whose endpoints are the two lifts ω', ω''. The specializations and generizations of D are therefore described by mutually disjoint oriented arcs of D̃ − {ω', ω''}. These arcs organise into polygonal (cyclic) structures, coming from the components D̃1, D̃2 of D̃ minus the two lifts.

Right column (page 5 of the notes). There is at least one specialization arc. The specialization–generization polygons have a definite number of vertices. Hence, in the graph Γ(Σ):
- Vertices are the classes D.
- Edges are immediate specializations.
- The set of immediate generizations of a vertex D (≃ Spec0(D), Comp0/Cosp0(D)) has a natural polygonal (cyclic) structure. This structure is tied to the set of orientations of D.
- The cardinality is at least 3, apparently more when D is special.
- A specialization D → D' relates the corresponding sets for D and D' through ω(D), ω(D'). The next page states that it gives an injection Gen1(D) ↪ Gen1(D') whose complement has two elements.
- NB: the set of generizations of D is identified with data attached to D∩S read on D̃ (orientation choices on D̃).

Purpose. These local cyclic orders are the 'rotation system' needed for the next page. There, Γ(Σ) is canonically cellularly embedded in a combinatorial surface Str(Σ), the stratified space of pseudo-lines relative to Σ. Vertices are classified as stable, semi-stable, critical and extremal. Edges and angular arcs carry weights whose sum around a vertex is 2n, since D̃ meets the n lifted pseudo-lines in 2n points.

In modern terms, Grothendieck is building the cell structure of the space of one-element pseudo-line extensions of a rank-3 arrangement (oriented matroid), i.e. its extension space. He is proving local 2-manifold structure by showing that the link of each vertex is a polygon.
errors: The page is too fragmentary to verify the counts. The previous page gives polygon order 4ν, corrected in a footnote to 2ν when only immediate generizations are counted. This page's lower bound (≥3, apparently more for special D) cannot be checked against a precise definition from the legible text.

The claim that the generization set carries a natural polygonal structure is asserted rather than proved here. It needs the disjointness of the specialization arcs on D̃ and a non-crossing argument that is only sketched.

ideas.what: Classes of a pseudo-line D relative to an arrangement Σ, related by immediate specialization (pushing D through a vertex) and generization.
ideas.modern_name: One-element (pseudo-line) extensions of a rank-3 oriented matroid, and their specialization order (the extension poset).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler, 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993).

ideas.what: The immediate generizations of D, read as disjoint oriented arcs on the double-cover circle D̃ between the lifts ω', ω'', carry a cyclic (polygon) structure.
ideas.modern_name: Link of a vertex in the cell decomposition of the extension space; rotation system for a cellular embedding.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) and the Bohne–Dress / Generalized Baues problem literature.

ideas.what: Graph Γ(Σ) of specializations, to be canonically cellularly embedded in a surface Str(Σ) (next page), with weights summing to 2n at each vertex.
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid as a 2-sphere / cellular surface; dual pseudo-line arrangement.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993): extension space has the homotopy type of a sphere for rank ≤3 (strongly euclidean case).

ideas.what: Using the double cover X̃ (sphere) and the lifted circle D̃ to handle orientations of pseudo-lines.
ideas.modern_name: Oriented-matroid / Folkman–Lawrence topological representation on S^2.

missed.claim: In 1983–84 Grothendieck was building, by hand, a canonical cell structure on the space of pseudo-line extensions of an arrangement. He shows that each vertex has a polygonal link, so that the specialization graph embeds cellularly in a surface. This anticipates the extension-space / Generalized Baues problem programme for rank 3 (Sturmfels–Ziegler 1993), where sphericity of the rank-3 extension space was proved later and without reference to him.
missed.quote: Il est muni d'une structure naturelle polygonale ... dans l'ens. des orientations de D
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: His direct combinatorial-surface approach (weights, stable/semi-stable/critical vertices, weight sum 2n) may give an explicit, local proof that the rank-3 extension space is a 2-manifold. It may also give a finer stratification than the oriented-matroid literature records. Historians of the Generalized Baues problem do not mention this.

missed.claim: The precise count of vertices of the specialization–generization polygons is left unsettled: 4ν versus 2ν on the previous page, and a lower bound of 3 or more here. The identification of Str(Σ) as a specific surface (sphere or projective plane) is also not stated on this page.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The local degree formula would give an Euler-characteristic computation of the extension space directly from Σ.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a substantive, mostly unknown construction: a cellular surface structure on the space of pseudo-line extensions, built via orientations on the double cover. It foreshadows results credited to Sturmfels–Ziegler about ten years later. The page itself is fragmentary and mostly local bookkeeping, so the surprise is moderate.
